issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and finality
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction over a final, appealable sentencing entry in both consolidated cases.

issues.label: Standard of review R.C. 2953.08(G)(2)
issues.why: The court must apply the correct statutory standard for reviewing felony sentences as “contrary to law” or unsupported findings.

issues.label: Effect of guilty pleas
issues.why: Guilty pleas waive many errors, so the court must identify which sentencing/constitutional claims survive the pleas.

issues.label: Merger/allied offenses analysis
issues.why: The court must determine whether any counts should have merged under R.C. 2941.25, affecting convictions and sentencing.

issues.label: Merger: involuntary manslaughter vs homicide
issues.why: The court must consider whether involuntary manslaughter and aggravated vehicular homicide for the same death are allied or otherwise duplicative.

issues.label: Merger: vehicular assault counts
issues.why: The court must assess whether the two vehicular-assault counts merge with each other or with homicide-related counts based on victims/animus.

issues.label: Merger: receiving stolen property overlap
issues.why: The court must consider whether receiving-stolen-property counts merge with predicate/related offenses where the same conduct/property is used.

issues.label: Merger: failure to stop after accident
issues.why: The court must determine whether multiple failure-to-stop counts were proper (e.g., per victim/vehicle/incident) or should merge.

issues.label: Merger: weapons/disability/ordnance counts
issues.why: The court must ensure any weapon-related counts/specs sentenced do not constitute multiple punishments for the same conduct.

issues.label: Dismissed counts/specs effect
issues.why: The court must verify sentencing reflects only counts/specifications to which Hampton pleaded guilty and that dismissals were honored.

issues.label: Sentencing range legality
issues.why: Each prison term must fall within the authorized statutory range for the degree of offense.

issues.label: Offense degree classification
issues.why: The court must confirm the correct felony degree was used for each conviction (including enhancements that change degree).

issues.label: Proper firearm-specification term
issues.why: The court must ensure the correct mandatory term was imposed for each firearm specification and that it is lawful for the offense.

issues.label: Spec consecutive-service mandate
issues.why: Firearm-specification time generally must be served prior to and consecutive to the base offense, requiring correct sequencing.

issues.label: Multiple firearm specs stacking
issues.why: The court must determine whether any firearm specifications could or could not be stacked consecutively under Ohio law.

issues.label: Dangerous ordnance classification
issues.why: The court must verify the “switch attachment”/3D-printed firearm legally qualifies as “dangerous ordnance” and supports the conviction/spec.

issues.label: Consecutive-sentencing findings
issues.why: If any non-mandatory consecutive terms were imposed, the court must make and journalize R.C. 2929.14(C)(4) findings.

issues.label: Consecutive-sentencing record support
issues.why: Appellate review must assess whether the consecutive findings are clearly and convincingly unsupported by the record under R.C. 2953.08(G)(2).

issues.label: Which terms are consecutive
issues.why: The court must correctly identify what was ordered consecutive (e.g., failure-to-comply term vs firearm spec vs other counts) and ensure clarity.

issues.label: Concurrent across cases legality
issues.why: The court must confirm it had authority to run the two case totals concurrently and did so in a lawful manner.

issues.label: Aggregate sentence calculation
issues.why: The total time must be correctly computed, including mandatory terms and any consecutive components.

issues.label: Postrelease control advisement
issues.why: The court must properly impose and notify Hampton of PRC for each felony at plea and at sentencing as required.

issues.label: PRC entry accuracy
issues.why: The sentencing entry must correctly state PRC terms/mandatory nature and consequences, or the sentence may be contrary to law.

issues.label: Jail-time credit determination
issues.why: The court must determine and journalize jail-time credit correctly, including credit allocation across concurrent/consecutive terms and both cases.

issues.label: Presentence investigation use
issues.why: The court must ensure it considered the PSI and that the record supports reliance on it without improper information.

issues.label: R.C. 2929.11 purposes/principles
issues.why: The court must consider felony sentencing purposes and principles and impose a sentence consistent with them.

issues.label: R.C. 2929.12 seriousness/recidivism
issues.why: The court must consider the statutory factors and avoid reliance on impermissible considerations.

issues.label: R.C. 2929.13 applicable guidance
issues.why: If any offense triggers R.C. 2929.13 provisions (mandatory prison or presumption), the court must comply.

issues.label: Mandatory prison terms beyond specs
issues.why: The court must determine whether any convictions carry mandatory prison (e.g., certain vehicular offenses/specs) and impose accordingly.

issues.label: Victim-impact statement rights
issues.why: The court must ensure victim/family statement procedures complied with law and did not inject impermissible punishment factors.

issues.label: Right of allocution
issues.why: The court must confirm Hampton was personally afforded allocution before sentence was imposed.

issues.label: Due process at sentencing
issues.why: The court must ensure sentencing was based on accurate information and Hampton had an opportunity to rebut disputed facts.

issues.label: Eighth Amendment proportionality
issues.why: The court must assess whether the aggregate sentence is grossly disproportionate under federal/Ohio constitutional standards.

issues.label: Ohio constitutional proportionality
issues.why: The court must apply Article I, Section 9/16 protections as interpreted by Ohio courts for felony sentencing challenges.

issues.label: Fifth Amendment/self-incrimination
issues.why: The court must consider whether sentencing penalized Hampton for silence or lack of admission beyond the plea.

issues.label: Fourteenth Amendment equal protection
issues.why: The court must ensure sentencing was not influenced by impermissible classifications or disparate treatment without rational basis.

issues.label: Fourteenth Amendment due process
issues.why: The court must assess whether the sentencing procedure met fundamental fairness, including notice of consequences and lawful penalties.

issues.label: Punishment for exercising rights
issues.why: The court must ensure Hampton was not punished for requesting trial (before plea), filing motions, or other protected conduct.

issues.label: Plea colloquy validity (Crim.R. 11)
issues.why: If Hampton’s claim implicates plea-based sentencing consequences, the court must ensure the pleas were knowing, intelligent, and voluntary.

issues.label: Notice of mandatory penalties at plea
issues.why: The court must confirm Hampton was advised of mandatory prison terms (e.g., firearm spec) and maximum penalties at the change-of-plea hearing.

issues.label: Sentencing entry conformity
issues.why: The court must ensure the written judgment matches the oral pronouncement and accurately states all terms/specs/forfeiture.

issues.label: Forfeiture specification procedure
issues.why: The court must verify lawful imposition of forfeiture, including identification of property, nexus, and proper order/journalization.

issues.label: Firearm/disposition forfeiture legality
issues.why: The court must ensure forfeiture of the 3D-printed firearm/switch complies with statutory forfeiture rules and due process.

issues.label: Costs, fines, restitution
issues.why: The court must address whether financial sanctions were imposed lawfully, with proper findings and notice (even if none, ensure omission is proper).

issues.label: Indigency and appointed counsel fees
issues.why: If counsel fees or costs are imposed, the court must ensure statutory requirements and ability-to-pay considerations are met.

issues.label: Failure-to-comply sentencing nuances
issues.why: The court must confirm the failure-to-comply count level and any statutory enhancement elements align with the plea and sentence imposed.

issues.label: Vehicular homicide/assault elements impact
issues.why: The court must ensure the sentencing level aligns with the specific subsection pleaded to and any requisite findings (e.g., mental state, OVI, reckless).

issues.label: Predicate felony for involuntary manslaughter
issues.why: The court must ensure the involuntary-manslaughter conviction rests on a valid underlying felony consistent with the plea and dismissal structure.

issues.label: Multiple-victim sentencing structure
issues.why: Where there are multiple victims (dead and seriously injured), the court must properly structure counts and sentences without double counting.

issues.label: Consolidation propriety impact
issues.why: The court must consider whether consolidation affected sentencing fairness or created spillover prejudice relevant to constitutional claims.

issues.label: Credit for time served on specs
issues.why: The court must ensure jail-time credit rules were not incorrectly applied to mandatory firearm-spec terms.

issues.label: Sentencing rationale on record
issues.why: While not always required, the court must avoid reversible error by ensuring any required findings/reasons are made where statutes demand them.

issues.label: Clerical errors and nunc pro tunc
issues.why: The court must identify whether any sentencing defects are clerical (correctable) or substantive (requiring resentencing).

issues.label: Remedy if sentence contrary to law
issues.why: The court must determine the proper appellate remedy—modify, vacate consecutive findings, remand for resentencing, or limited correction.
